next_engineering_direction: A real lifetime change must stop submitting one whole lazy graph with all block intermediates at once. Use a native-completion-driven bounded number of block evaluations: precompile full/tail block math, submit from the existing owner stream, retire prior temporary roots only on actual GPU completion, then enqueue the next block on that owner thread. Keep one user Completion and the O(output) result frontier. This needs a native retirement/event adapter and invocation-state/lifetime design, not another depends or per-block host synchronize/wait. An explicit reusable-workspace native plan is an alternative if output/scratch binding exists. Same full KV and F32 arithmetic/work must remain; no new shader/precision reduction is implied. Only a future design direction, not implemented or proven feasible with current public MLX hooks.
